subject: Is it possible to have axis appear as percent (e.g. 55%) rather than just decimal (.55)?

messages.author: d5a6de7022197614
messages.subject: Is it possible to have axis appear as percent (e.g. 55%) rather than just decimal (.55)?
parts:
Hi All,
 
I've been unsuccessful in solving the seemingly simple and common problem of displaying my y axis as percentages (55%) instead of decimals (.55). First, is it possible in ggplot, and second, (I assume it is possible) what's involved?
 
Thanks,
-Gary

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to have axis appear as percent (e.g. 55%) rather than just decimal (.55)?
parts:
Use the formatteer argument in scale_continuous.

p + scale_y_continuous(formatter = "percent")

HTH
Luciano

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to have axis appear as percent (e.g. 55%) rather than just decimal (.55)?
parts:
In the forthcoming version of ggplot2 (0.9.0), the functions used to
produce formatted scales are transferred to the scales package. In the
future, this will be the specification as shown in the example below,
which works in the development version of 0.9.0:

d <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = sample(30:80, 10, replace = FALSE))
library('ggplot2')
library('scales')
ggplot(d, aes(x, y/100)) + geom_point() +
ylab('y') + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent)

In the scales package, format_percent() is a formatting function
(which is why it is not quoted above), and the argument will become
labels = rather than formatter =. This will be described in the help
page of ggplot2::scale_y_continuous (and is already present in the
development version).

However, the above does not work in the current version (0.8.9):

> ggplot(d, aes(x, y/100)) + geom_point() +
+ ylab('y') + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent)
Error: Labels can only be specified in conjunction with breaks

so at present, Luciano's code is correct. This is to inform that
changes will soon be coming in certain aspects of ggplot2, including
the way axis and legends are specified. For example, with respect to
scales, both breaks and labels will be allowed to take functions as
arguments.

Dennis
